systems.result: hotter summer strongly reduces floral cyanidin and summer-white flowers downregulate overlapping pigment-network nodes

systems.interaction_type: pigment genotype x experimental temperature fitness
systems.result: CHS-null white genotype has approximately 24-26% lower fertilization success than pigmented genotype in high-temperature conditions, not at low temperature

systems.interaction_type: natural thermal cline plus known pigment mechanism
systems.result: white frequency increases with growing-season temperature; white petals show strong CHS downregulation

systems.interaction_type: natural colour morph x thermal condition
systems.result: pink morph is associated with warmer conditions and white with colder/winter conditions; direction opposes universal hotter-to-white rule

general_hypothesis: pigment-network genotype/regulatory state x temperature, not a universal temperature main effect
prediction: cross-species variance in genotype/morph-by-temperature interactions should be substantial and linked to the affected pigment-network node
hard_nonclaims: does not establish a universal direction of temperature-driven colour change
does not rescue failed cross-cohort BIO5 replication
Ipomoea experiment tests fitness consequences rather than heat-induced flower whitening
